followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and preference fit.

**Capability:** This is essentially a factual recall and structured-listing task. Plover leads Willet meaningfully on the relevant metrics — Extraction & Retrieval (85.3 vs 78.5) and general knowledge via MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 75.4). Those gaps are well outside the run-to-run variance threshold, so Plover is the stronger choice for getting the content right.

**Tone/preference:** The user's phrasing ("don't ramble like last time — just get it right") is mildly hostile and adversarial. Willet's documentation says its self-reported preference declines as request warmth decreases, while Plover's preference response to tone is flat. Since these are only self-reported preferences with no documented effect on output quality, this was a secondary factor — but it pointed the same direction as the capability analysis, so it reinforced the call rather than complicating it.

Both signals favored Plover, so it was a clean decision.
